items.title: Max Verstappen Spent 40 Hours Playing GTA 6 and Still Won the Las Vegas Grand Prix
items.description: Famous Dutch-Belgian race driver Max Verstappen revealed that he’d spent the weekend of the Las Vegas Grand Prix locked in to GTA 6, saying he played over 40 hours of the game.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Famous Dutch-Belgian race driver Max Verstappen revealed that he’d spent the weekend of the Las Vegas Grand Prix locked in to GTA 6, saying he played over 40 hours of the game.

Everyone’s got GTA 6 fever, including Max Verstappen. Not even the Las Vegas Grand Prix could stop him from causing virtual chaos in Vice City, which he says he spent more than 40 hours doing during the weekend of the race.

Verstappen nonchalantly dropped this nugget of information during a live stream the following week, saying he would play the game in the mornings and evenings in between his duties on the track.

“I played a lot in the evening and in the morning in Vegas,” Verstappen explained. “I mean, I can’t go out anyways and walk around.”

The driver also revealed that he’s been so focused on GTA 6 and driving real-life race cars that he’s “completely forgotten” how to play Minecraft, despite having a scheduled stream for it.

“I’m so bad when I play too many games at the same time. I can’t, I just can’t!” he joked.

🤯Max Verstappen played GTA VI for FORTY HOURS while in Las Vegas

On top of that, he also won the race https://t.co/jwuxQnHxyS

— Pablo Martinez (Holiness) (@F1BigData) November 24, 2026

The Las Vegas Grand Prix took place on November 19 - 21. Verstappen took first place in the prestigious Formula 1 race, beating out Britain’s Lando Norris and Australia’s Oscar Piastri. The race is around 50 laps long with a total race distance of 192.6 miles (309.96 kilometers), generally lasting around one and a half hours.

As revealed by the name, Grand Theft Auto is a game series that involves a lot of vehicles, and not just for carjacking; the latest entry in the franchise even features drag racing and mudding, a hobby common in the American countryside that involves the use of off-road vehicles racing through mud-covered areas or even specially-made racetracks.

It’s quite likely that Verstappen dabbled a bit in these side missions, though he says that he’s already beaten 80% of GTA 6’s story. In fact, the driver admitted that he has skipped most of the main cutscenes, calling them “too boring.”

Verstappen’s style of playing GTA 6 is one of several that we’ve seen over the weekend. In fact, many players are avoiding progressing the story in favor of spending time in Chapter 1, which sees Jason living the average life of a drug runner in Rockstar’s fictionalized version of the Florida Keys. Oddly, it’s a slow-paced, slice-of-life section of the game that some players haven’t left yet, preferring to take it easy diving for treasure, fishing with Cal, and soaking up the environment.

If you're already driving all around Leonida and want to know everything there is to find and do, see the Leonida interactive map.

items.title: Some GTA 6 Fans Love Chapter 1 for Its Slower Pace and Are Spending Dozens of Hours Roleplaying in It
items.description: GTA 6's first chapter has been somewhat divisive due to its slower pace, but it's also a part of the game that some fans have spent dozens of hours playing due to it highly immersive slice-of-life elements.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Warning: This article features light spoilers for the early hours of GTA 6.

GTA 6's first chapter has been somewhat divisive due to its slower pace, but it's also a part of the game that some fans have spent dozens of hours playing due to it highly immersive slice-of-life elements.

Instead of throwing you headfirst into crazy heists or explosive set pieces, the first chapter of GTA 6 is largely spent bumbling around Rockstar's version of the Florida Keys. You can go fishing, scuba diving, and even fix up your house before Lucia's release from prison. It's an exceptionally low-key and chill opening to a game filled with all kinds of crazy action, which is why it's also rubbed some people the wrong way. They don't want to do chores or kick it on the beach; they want to cause some mayhem.

However, for others, this has become an unexpected hook for GTA 6 that actually delayed their interest in getting to the meat of Rockstar's open-world epic. Various fans of the game have said they spent anywhere from 10 to as many as 40+ hours in just Chapter 1 alone. Keep in mind, this is a sliver of the overall experience, and much of the game's most interesting activities don't get added until subsequent chapters. However, some players just enjoyed living inside of this part of the game before things go horribly wrong and they're forced to start ramping up the violence and crime.

"Best thing about that early chapter is just how low stakes and casual it feels," said X user @CS11__ after spending 41 hours in Chapter 1 alone. "I forced myself not to go farther than Hamlet, so I really only ever experienced these two small areas in 40 hours. [...] The game hardly opened up, but it still felt unbelievably rich and fun."

But... what is it these people are actually doing, if not blowing stuff up and creating tons of chaos? Some fans were just going through the motions, giving themselves daily routines that involved working out, taking on relaxing hobbies, and exploring.

"[A] lot of roleplaying, day-to-day living type stuff," said Aaron Espionza on X, who estimated that he spent around 15–18 hours before picking up Lucia from prison. "I had a routine even when I would wake up, drive to the juice bar down the street, get my orange juice, and then say hello to the locals. If anyone said anything mean, I would get violent and throw empty juice cups at them. [I] did the workout routines. Basketball was a favorite of mine. Side stuff with Cal fishing, Donnie pick-ups, and scuba. But so much of it was testing how much detail Rockstar put into it. 'If I do this, will they do that?' type of systems exploration. Always came away surprised."

X user @scaasm noted that the lower stakes nature of Chapter 1 even prompted him to follow traffic laws and use manual turn signals in GTA 6: "I follow traffic laws unless I'm doing something criminal, and generally just taking it very slow. [I'm] loving every moment."

The location itself was also a big driving point for a lot of fans, some of whom have personal connections or apprecation for its real life counterpart: "As someone from Florida, I think the Keys is one of those locations that they absolutely nailed (waning sands outlets too; they look exactly like the Orlando ones)," said @piterparker69 on X. "It felt kinda uncanny driving around (especially the 7 Mile Bridge) because of how good it replicates real life."

"I have been obsessed with the Florida Keys for the last 5 years, and finding out you spend the start of the game there, catching fish, fixing my house, working out, and just vibing gave me little motivation to move on," said @AnchormanV2 on X after spending roughly a dozen hours in Chapter 1.

"I took my sweet time in Key Lento, not necessarily to avoid progressing the story, but more so [bcause] I was just having so much fun exploring the keys and just taking it all in," said X user @HorrorUntitled. "There’s just so much to see to see and happening. It’s very overwhelming."

Of course, some people did get into a bit of open-world crime as well, or explore a bit beyond the Keys, but a lot of it was still a result of the story feeling low-stakes and not having much urgency in its first chaper. X user Ryan Ranc even noted that he would go around Key Lento acting as a vigilante: "I’m playing as Batman and roaming at night on my motorbike stopping crime."

Chapter 1 in GTA 6 is a very interesting piece of the game, and some even noted that they longed for that tranquility after moving on in the story. It's an intentional slow burn, as things get turned up to an 11 at the end of the chapter and make you come to appreciate what you had. It's the calm before the storm in many ways, and some people are really basking in that.

items.title: Diablo 4 Season 16 Fixes One of the Biggest Problems With Helltide
items.description: Diablo 4 Season 16: Season of Tyrael's Gambit officially kicks off on December 1. We finally know a bit more about what the new season holds in store, and it's going to make one of the biggest activities much less of a pain.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
Diablo 4 Season 16: Season of Tyrael's Gambit officially kicks off on December 1. We finally know a bit more about what the new season holds in store, and it's going to make one of the biggest activities much less of a pain.

Season 15, Hell's Legacy, is a tough act to follow. It brought in a ton of nostalgic content like the Prime Evils, runewords, and even Whimsyshire. It does seem like a lot of that anniversary content is going to be retired (I'll miss runewords), but at least it seems like Season of Tyrael's Gambit is going to make farming Helltides a bit less annoying.

In the patch notes for the new season, Blizzard says one Helltide will always be up in the vanilla zones, with another active in either Nahantu or Skovos, offset by 30 minutes. In practice, that means there will always be an active Helltide. That would be good enough on its own, but Blizzard is also changing the way Abberant Cinders work. Instead of expiring at the end of each Helltide, Blizzard is introducing a cap, and will let you carry cinders between Helltides.

For the uninitiated, that might not seem like a big deal, but it's a massive quality-of-life change. If you're not aware, Helltide is essentially an in-game invasion event, where demons overrun an area in the open world. You go in and kill demons for 55 minutes to get Abberant Cinders, which you can then use to unlock chests scattered throughout the zone. Helltides have always been one of the best ways to farm XP, and there have been several seasons that revolve entirely around them.

Now that War Plans, which were introduced with Lord of Hatred, are such a central part of how Diablo 4's gameplay loop works, there's always a chance that you're going to need to do bit of Helltide farming to progress. The problem was that Helltides spawned on a timer, and there was always a 5-minute gap between them. That doesn't sound too bad, but sometimes a Helltide would pop up in your to-do list and you'd either zone in with a mere 10 minutes to gather a ton of Cinders, or there simply wouldn't be a Helltide active. This new change solves both of those problems.

Now, even if you go into a Helltide with just a few minutes remaining, you can still gather Cinders without having to worry about opening 250 Cinders worth of chests before the timer expires. You can simply farm until the Helltide moves and then teleport to the next one. Easy. It's such a seemingly small change, but it's made me more excited for the 16th season of this ARPG than anything I've heard about it so far.

Beyond that, the Season of Tyrael's Gambit also brings changes to War Plans, where you'll be able to customize them to favor the activities you actually like doing. So, if you hate Helltide, even with the new changes, it sounds like you'll be able to make them appear a little less often in your War Plans.

The new season will also have a new item type called Horadric Items, which will synergize with set talismans. In the example Blizzard shared in its post, this could be as simple as adding +1 set count to your talismans to an ability that is only activated if you have a certain set of talismans equipped.

Seasons like this are a prime example of the way Blizzard will support Diablo 4 going forward, now that Diablo 5 is in the works. Diablo 4's director has come out and reassured fans that the game will continue to get new seasons as long as people are playing, and with how different Diablo 5 sounds so far, it's possible that Diablo 4 will have a long life ahead of it.

items.title: The Witcher 4 Will Have a Comparable Leap From GTA 5 to GTA 6, Says CD Projekt Red
items.description: CD Projekt Red expects a leap between The Witcher 3 and 4 that is comparable to the one between GTA 5 and 6.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
CD Projekt Red expects a leap between The Witcher 3 and 4 that is comparable to the one between GTA 5 and 6.

In a recent earnings call (via Eurogamer), CDPR was peppered with questions about GTA 6, since the developer also makes ambitious open-world games. CDPR joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski was asked whether or not the studio is looking at GTA for inspiration and if people can expect a similar leap between games. He noted that they have, indeed, observed the jump between GTA 5 and 6 before stating that fans can expect something comparable for The Witcher 4.

"We believe there's going to be a comparable leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4 — I think so, yes," he said. "It's been 11 years, we are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game, so yes, you should expect us to make a much bigger jump between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4."

The leap between GTA 5 and 6 is pretty absurd. There's a significant number of more things to do, particularly for those interested in roleplaying as a criminal. You can steal drugs, rob banks, knock over virtually any store on the map, and so much more. A lot of these details were either reserved for scripted missions in GTA 5 or were underbaked as open-world activities, but are fully fleshed out for you to do however you want in GTA 6. Advancements in NPCs, interactivity, immersion, and the ability to enter hundreds of interiors also make GTA 6 feel a world apart from its predecessor.

Will The Witcher 4 also have tons of enterable interiors or deeper interactions with random NPCs? It's too soon to tell. It's possible that the leap for CD Projekt Red could come in a number of other ways, as The Witcher is a totally different world from GTA, after all. Maybe monster hunting will be more nuanced and involved than in The Witcher 3, similar to how GTA 6 has more engaging criminal activities.

CDPR also noted that it plans to find ways to expand the game to more mainstream audiences, like GTA 6 has. GTA 6 collaborated with major mainstream artists to create original music, in addition to bold marketing campaigns that made the game difficult to ignore.

The Witcher 4 is currently targeting a 2028 release, and we can probably expect more looks at the game next year. CDPR also noted that it has signed a marketing agreement with PlayStation for the game, which will also cover previous games and allow for opportunities with PlayStation Plus' services.

media:description.$text:
Polaris, aka The Witcher 4

CD Projekt Red confirmed that a new Witcher game that would mark the beginning of a new saga was in development in March 2022, and though it's not officially called The Witcher 4, this one can be thought of as the true next Witcher game.

Later revealed to be codenamed Polaris, the new game won't be released until 2025 at the earliest as it only entered pre-production in May 2022. It's also being developed in Unreal Engine 5, a new endeavour for CD Projekt Red that's essentially requiring them to create everything from the ground-up and establish a new foundation for its games going forward. It will, however, be one of the next two games released by CD Projekt Red.

(Image: CD Projekt Red)

items.title: 'Crazy Secretive' — GTA 6 Voice Actor Reveals Details of Rockstar's 'Humongous' NDA
items.description: A voice actor who appeared in GTA 6 described the wild non-disclosure agreement she had to sign before working on the game, calling the project “crazy secretive.”
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
A voice actor who appeared in GTA 6 described the wild non-disclosure agreement she had to sign before working on the game, calling the project “crazy secretive.”

Issa Lopez is a voice actor who plays a radio host on GTA 6’s fictional Cocoteo FM radio station, a Latin channel that plays reggaeton and dembow tracks featuring Spanish-speaking artists from the Caribbean and Latin America.

In a November 20 interview with Page Six, Lopez revealed that she recorded her lines for the station as recently as September 2026, and said the NDA she was made to sign before officially performing the part was comparable to the process of purchasing a home or a vehicle.

“Have you ever signed papers to buy a house? To buy a car? You know, it’s thick! It was a pretty humongous pack of papers that came with it. But I mean, it’s worth it! And I didn’t have to wait like all these other folks. Some of these folks have been working on this for like 10–11 years, you know what I mean?” she said.

She went on to describe the recording process for her lines, saying that she hadn’t seen anything until the day of the performance. With no time to prepare, she was essentially “put on the spot” — but she was so excited about the opportunity that she didn’t mind.

“In my usual voiceover gigs — let’s say you want me to do a commercial for you. I get a Zoom [link] maybe the day before, maybe the same day I get the script,” she explained. “Everything was like, popped up on the screen. It was mad cool. It was like, ‘You ready? And I’m like, ‘Uh-huh.’ You press a button and then boop, it pops on the screen, they say hello, and there’s a bunch of people in your ear. items.title: Cyberpunk 2 Is Still a Ways Out, but CD Projekt Red Says Its RPGs Will Come Out Faster in the Future
items.description: We are still two years out from The Witcher 4, but Ciri's big breakout adventure isn't the only massive RPG cooking at CD Projekt Red. It sounds like development on Cyberpunk 2 is carrying on smoothly, though it's still very early in its development cycle.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
We are still two years out from The Witcher 4, but Ciri's big breakout adventure isn't the only massive RPG cooking at CD Projekt Red. It sounds like development on Cyberpunk 2 is carrying on smoothly, though it's still very early in its development cycle.

In a November 24 earnings call, CD Projekt Red VP of Strategy & Investor Relations Karolina Gnaś said the team is "making good progress with Cyberpunk 2, we are happy with where we are, but it's still too early to give a specific date and plan on when we will move onto full production." Although she couldn't provide a clear date when we'll hear more about the game, she did add that the studio plans to have around 200 developers by the end of 2026 and 320 by the end of next year.

It is admittedly a bit early to expect any kind of information about the Cyberpunk sequel, but it has been simmering in the background since at least 2022, and it sounds like CD Projekt Red wants to speed up development of its massive RPGs. In its consolidated earnings report, CD Projekt Red admitted that most of its games "normally take 3 to 6 years to produce," mostly due to working on one game at a time. But that strategy has since changed.

In that same report, the company said, "At the moment, the CD Projekt Red studio is working in parallel on several productions (also in collaboration with external development teams) and supporting products, which is expected to translate into shorter intervals between the releases of subsequent titles in the future." Whether or not that new timeline will affect Cyberpunk 2 is the question.

But even if that faster development timeline is in effect for Cyberpunk 2, it's likely we'll still have to wait a while to actually see it in the wild. In an earnings report last year, when Cyberpunk 2 entered pre-production, CD Projekt CEO Michał Nowakowski suggested that CDPR's games take four or five years to move from pre-production to release, which would put the game somewhere in 2030 or 2031. And given that the game still hasn't entered full production, it isn't likely we're going to see some sort of rapid release after the Witcher 4 in 2028.

We're probably going to be waiting a little while longer for Cyberpunk 2, but it's already sounding like the game is taking shape. Just last month, associate game director Pawel Sasko revealed that a lot of the developers working on Cyberpunk 2 are former modders. Sasko went on to claim that "the modding community is really keeping [Cyberpunk 2077] alive," so hopefully that energy translates to Cyberpunk 2 – whenever it comes out.

items.title: PlayStation Secures Marketing Agreement for The Witcher 4
items.description: CD Projekt Red has signed a marketing deal with PlayStation for The Witcher 4.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
CD Projekt Red has signed a marketing deal with PlayStation for The Witcher 4.

The studio confirmed the deal in its latest earnings report, which may also suggest that marketing is about to ramp up. Additionally, CD Projekt Red noted that this partnership will "cover the presence" of its games on PlayStation and PlayStation Plus, which likely means older titles like The Witcher 3 or Cyberpunk 2077 may make their way to the subscription service in the future.

“Just today, we signed new partnership agreements with Sony Interactive Entertainment covering the presence of our games on PlayStation and in PlayStation Plus subscriptions, as well as our collaboration during the upcoming Witcher 4 marketing campaign,” said Piotr Nielubowicz, chief financial officer at CDPR. "This cooperation will support our business and financial outlook in this and future years.”

It wouldn't be surprising if PlayStation uses this agreement to make The Witcher 3 available through PlayStation Plus when the game's new expansion releases in 2027. This deal may also mean that The Witcher 4 has a big presence in a future State of Play stream, though no hard specifics were revealed by CD Projekt Red. Currently, the game is due out in 2028, so new trailers and gameplay seem likely next year.

The decision also signals an end of an era, to a degree. CD Projekt Red has had a strong relationship with Xbox since The Witcher 3. The game was prominently featured during Xbox's E3 showcases, and that continued with Cyberpunk 2077, even resulting in a special edition Xbox One X console themed after the game. Given PlayStation has a larger user base than Xbox this generation, it makes sense why CDPR may be interested in working with them.

Marketing deals can be extremely effective when done right. In the case of GTA 6, a lot of people bought PlayStation 5s instead of an Xbox, since Rockstar and Sony marketed the console as the "best place to play" the game. This led to the game being the biggest launch in PlayStation's history, with 39 million people playing it on PS5. 70% of people who bought a new PS5 during the last week also booted up GTA 6 as their first game.

items.title: Over Half of GTA 6 Watch Time Came From Viewers Under 25 Years Old
items.description: The bulk of fans watching streams of GTA 6 are under 25 years old, according to recent stats compiled by StreamsCharts.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
The bulk of fans watching streams of GTA 6 are under 25 years old, according to recent stats compiled by StreamsCharts.

After 13 long years, GTA 6 is finally out in the wild. Rockstar’s highly anticipated release has already broken numerous records, one of the most impressive being that it became the single most popular game ever on both Twitch and Kick just 26 hours after its global release.

Now that it’s had a little time to breathe, more data is rolling in, including information about who’s watching streamers play the game. StreamsCharts, a data analytics company that studies games-focused streaming platforms, discovered that most viewers of GTA 6 broadcasts tend to trend under the age of 25.

According to Streamlabs’ stats, 30.8% of viewers in GTA 6 streams are 20 - 24 years old, making up the bulk of those watching the game across Kick, Twitch, and YouTube. (Painfully, StreamsCharts pointed out that these players were in elementary school when GTA 5 came out.) 16.8% of these viewers are 17 - 19, with 8.5% accounting for viewers 16 or under. The second-largest age range watching GTA 6 streams are viewers aged 25–29. 11.6% of viewers are 30–34, and the numbers keep dropping from there.

StreamsCharts also found that an overwhelming majority of these viewers are single men, accounting for 83.8% of the gender divide. That’s not to say that gals aren’t also watching streamers play Rockstar’s latest; 14% of viewers are female, and if you’ve been on social media lately, you’ve probably seen a fair few female players showing off their outfits for Jason and Lucia or the viral conversation about how it’s, oddly, comparable to a crime-focused version of The Sims.

Perhaps unsurprisingly, the United States makes up the bulk of GTA 6 viewership. Brazil isn’t far behind, coming in at 12.4% of the game’s total audience; Spain and Germany follow at 6.9% and 6.8%, respectively.

Certain games have also experienced a drop in viewership following GTA 6’s release. StreamsCharts found that GTA 5 had the sharpest drop-off on Twitch, followed by the platform’s Just Chatting category and World of Warcraft.

The GTA hype train is in full swing, and it’s making big bucks for Rockstar. The company reportedly made a staggering $3.79 billion from the game in just 24 hours, making it the single biggest entertainment launch in history. Internet provider Comcast even revealed that it experienced its highest-traffic day ever as players downloaded the game to their consoles, and PlayStation confirmed that GTA 6 was its biggest game launch in the company’s history.

items.title: Kevin Feige and the Russo Brothers are Planning a Special Tribute to Patrick Stewart as Avengers: Doomsday Release Approaches
items.description: Marvel Studios boss Kevin Feige has revealed that he and the Russo brothers are creating a tribute to honor the late great Patrick Stewart in light of his final performance in Avengers: Doomsday.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Marvel Studios boss Kevin Feige has revealed that he and the Russo brothers are creating a tribute to honor the late great Patrick Stewart in light of his final performance in Avengers: Doomsday.

Sir Patrick Stewart died at the age of 86 on October 28, 2026. The prolific actor’s death followed a brief battle with Alzheimer's and Lewy Body Dementia, prompting a period of mourning from both fans and fellow collaborators, the latter of whom shared fond memories from their time working with the Star Trek and X-Men alum on social media.

Speaking with Entertainment Weekly ahead of Avengers: Doomsday’s December release, Kevin Feige revealed that he and the Russo brothers are working on creating a tribute to Stewart, given his many years playing Charles Xavier in the X-Men films.

“We’re long done filming that movie [Doomsday], and he did an amazing job for us,” Feige told the outlet. “We’re looking now at how we can put something together that honors and respects our friend.”

In that same interview, Joseph Russo reflected on Stewart’s role in the upcoming film, revealing that the actor shared a particularly moving scene with his fellow thespian and real-life best friend, Ian McKellan. (I’m growing misty-eyed as I type this; McKellan shared a touching statement about his late friend shortly after the news broke, saying he “wore his heart on his sleeve, which made him a man to rely on, to admire and in my case, love.")

“In a lot of ways, Xavier’s the conscience in the movie,” Joseph Russo revealed. “He has a lovely scene with Ian McKellen, who’s his best friend, in the film. It’s a very emotional scene about forgiveness, and I think very resonant in the wake of his passing.”

Anthony Russo went on to share an anecdote about his time working with Stewart on the set of Doomsday, saying the actor did his best to put on a good show in spite of his failing health.

“It was clear that he was struggling with his health, and he worked so hard to deliver a performance and a presence — for us as directors, for his other actors, for the crew,” Anthony said. “You could see it wasn’t just the effort of a regular actor showing up and delivering that kind of presence and performance and experience for others, collaboration. It was someone who was really being challenged in a very deep way on a health level, showing up and doing that. For him to have muscled through and delivered the performance that he did in that movie, and the experience that he delivered for all of us as collaborators, it made it intensely emotional.”

Avengers: Doomsday marks Patrick Stewart’s final film performance. The knighted actor was best known for playing Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek and Charles Xavier in the X-Men films of the 2010s, but also lent his talents to numerous memorable voiceover roles, such as Emperor Uriel Septim VII in the Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion and Lord Yupa in Studio Ghibli’s Nausicaa of the Valley of the Wind.

Avengers: Doomsday releases in theaters on December 18, 2026. For more news about this forthcoming superhero flick, check out what we learned from its “final” trailer, and peep the parallels fans discovered between the latest Doctor Doom poster and another early promotional Iron Man poster.

items.title: Walmart Now Lets Meta’s Muse AI Agent Shop for You During Black Friday
items.author: Chris Reed
items.content:
Ready or not, the world of agentic AI is descending upon us. From Meta’s Muse to OpenAI’s Dots, a number of artificial intelligence companies have released digital “agents” that have capabilities beyond just answering questions in a chat window. These AI assistants can actually do things for you, either in the cloud or directly on your computer. One of those things is shopping.

Some retailers are putting up barriers to make sure AI bots can’t shop on their websites. Walmart is going the other way and embracing the AI-bot-shopping future. Just in time for Black Friday, the mega-retailer has set up Agent Profiles and the Walmart Agent Gateway, which allow digital agents to shop on behalf of customers, within certain limitations. Muse intigration with your Walmart account is now available.

With Agent Profiles, Walmart’s system knows your Muse agent is shopping on your behalf, and won’t mistake its actions for yours. The profile also lets you track which items your agent has purchased separately from those you've bought yourself.

Muse won’t have access to your shopping history or other personal information known to Walmart. You can set additional guardrails around your Muse agent, like giving it a spending limit, and requiring it to ask for manual approval before completing purchases. You can also delete the agent’s profile at any time.

If you want to try it out, you can do so in the Muse app. First you’ll be asked to sign into your Walmart account, and then brought back to Muse, where you can ask it to compare products or find deals on items you’re interested in buying. It can add items to your cart and use your saved payment information to check out, if you let it.

I tried the Walmart integration this morning by asking Muse to add an item to my cart. Instead of using the official Walmart Agent Gateway and creating an Agent Profile, it opened a virtual browser and added the item to a guest cart on Walmart's site, set for pickup at a store I didn’t recognize.

I then asked Muse if it had official Walmart integration, and it confirmed that it did. Only then did it offer me the new sign-in option. So you may need to specifically ask for it if you want to try it yourself.

On the other hand, if you want to do it old-school and peruse Walmart's Black Friday 2026 sale personally and without an AI agent, I don't blame you one bit.

items.title: GTA 6 Gets Officially Licensed Trading Cards Based on In-Game Collectibles
items.description: Rockstar is teaming up with Panini America to bring the hunt for GTA 6 trading cards to life.
items.author: Blythe Dujardin
items.content:
The hunt for GTA 6 trading cards is leaving the virtual confines of Leonida — Rockstar is teaming up with Panini America to bring the in-game collectibles to life.

The officially licensed GTA 6: Sports Trading Card Collection is based on Panini’s standard sports card system, featuring rare-numbered cards and team color parallels. The GTA collection adds Vice City-specific Silver, Pink, Teal, and Light Blue parallels to the standard slate of Legend Bronze, Silver, and Gold.

The collectible company has revealed images of several cards planned for the collaboration, which is set to launch this December.

The Panini Group is an Italian-based collectible company that’s become quite the household name for sports card fans. Panini America is the official collectible partner for leagues like the WNBA, NASCAR, and FIFA, just to name a few.

GTA 6 cards will be released in four-pack boxes, each of which, on average, come with two Rookies, one Retro, one Illustrated, and four Special Silvers. There’s no word on pricing, but hobby boxes currently listed on Panini’s site start at $30 and go up to over $700.

Panini’s card images, shown above, feature a collection of fictional athletes from Vice City’s sports teams. Not all of the featured athletes are entirely fake — for instance, Tyreek Hill, ex-wide receiver for the Miami Dolphins, serves as the voice and likeness for the Vice City Manatees’ Maleek Rivers.

GTA 6 features a total of 480 trading cards across 16 individual sets, and we don't know exactly how many Panini is planning to turn into real cardboard. The sports-focused collectible company is less likely to adapt the collectible cards featuring other GTA 6 characters like Mandy and Vicki, but social media users can hope.

items.title: Rings of Power Renewed by Amazon for Season 4
items.description: The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 wraps up later tonight, but the show has already been renewed for Season 4 at Prime Video.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 wraps up later tonight, but the show has already been renewed for Season 4 at Prime Video.

Amazon MGM has renewed Rings of Power just as the show has wrapped up its third season, according to a report from Variety. The new season will continue the show's exploration of Middle-earth's second age, and will begin filming in spring 2027, though no release date has been announced yet.

While the show has been divisive for Tolkien fans, Amazon MGM's head of global television, Peter Friedlander, tells Variety that, "The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power has become a defining series for Prime Video." He also says that after the finale of Season 3 delivered "the landmark moment fans have been waiting for," the studio looks forward to "bringing fans even deeper into the rich world of Tolkien's Second Age."

Thus far, the third season seems to be an improvement. Here at IGN, we gave the last three episodes of the show a 7 out of 10, with reviewer Jim Vejvoda saying, "The Rings of Power loses some forward momentum this week with two very talky episodes where several characters are literally waiting around for something to happen." However, the first half of the season was much stronger, with Jim giving the first four episodes an 8, saying "The Rings of Power Season 3, Episodes 1-4 prove a welcome return to Middle-earth, allowing the series to get back on track after two seasons of wandering."

However, as the show nears the war that ends the Second Age of Middle-earth, it's going to be interesting to see where the showrunners take Rings of Power next season. There is a good chunk of time between the forging of the One Ring and the War of the Last Alliance that kicked off the Third Age, but no matter where they go with it, it'll likely involve the expanding influence of Sauron. We might even get another time jump.

It'll also be interesting to see if Prime Video takes the same approach to the show's release as it did with Season 3, releasing the episodes in blocks of three, likely to lure in new subscribers during Black Friday. We've also explored where all the rings are in Season 3 of The Rings of Power, and explained the massive time jump that starts off the season.

items.title: Wizards of the Coast Sues Website That Prints Fake Magic: The Gathering Cards, Alleging Counterfeiting Operation
items.description: For as much as Magic: The Gathering has grown in popularity over the last several years, the market for proxies and counterfeits has also grown. And now, Wizards of the Coast is suing PrintMTG, alleging a counterfeiting ring for the trading card game.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
For as much as Magic: The Gathering has grown in popularity over the last several years, the market for proxies and counterfeits has also grown. And now, Wizards of the Coast is suing PrintMTG, alleging a counterfeiting ring for the trading card game.

Wizards of the Coast filed the lawsuit (via Aftermath) in its home state of Washington, alleging PrintMTG "operate as a complex and sophisticated network (...) engaged in trademark infringement, counterfeiting and criminal copyright infringement on a grand scale." Wizards seeks $28.65 million in damages.

For the most part, PrintMTG was a destination for people to print proxies, or essentially fake Magic cards that could stand in for real ones, for either playtesting or trying before you buy the actual card. And, thanks to the Reserved list, there are plenty of cards that cost thousands of dollars for a legitimate copy, so it's easy to see why going to a website and spending $0.75 on a proxy version instead was a popular choice.

In its complaint, Wizards of the Coast seems to acknowledge the purpose that proxies serve, saying "an honest proxy is a stand-in for a real card that makes no claim to authenticity by appearance or otherwise. Though proxies are prohibited in all sanctioned Magic events, Wizards recognizes that private and noncommercial proxying is a vehicle players can use to further engage with the game, not to undermine it." But, it seems PrintMTG proxies were a bit too realistic.

Later on in the complaint, Wizards of the Coast describes what it sees as a legitimate proxy, which "include writing the name of a card in marker on a basic land card or on a blank card printed for this purpose, using one genuine card to represent another or sliding a slip of notebook paper into a card sleeve." PrintMTG and other proxy-printing websites like it, will instead print Magic's art on card stock, for a price.

Wizards of the Coast alleges that PrintMTG's proxies "directly harm Wizards by displacing sales of genuine cards" and damages "retail partners who sell those cards." But even beyond that, the company alleges that these counterfeits were "creating instability and uncertainty in the very secondary markets third-party retailers rely on as a revenue center."

There's a whole Reddit community that's sprung up, /r/RealOrNotTCG, where people post pictures of Magic cards to try and figure out if they're, well, real or not. However, PrintMTG is just one of many services that print realistic Magic proxies. This is a market that's been around for years, and it seems like Wizards of the Coast is finally cracking down on it.

This lawsuit comes after Wizards of the Coast recently changed the way booster packs work, and ahead of Darkhold Destiny, its third Marvel set.

items.title: Marvel Shows Off First Look at Kelsey Grammer's Beast in Avengers: Doomsday, and Fans Are Divided
items.description: We’ve gotten our first look at Kelsey Grammer’s Beast as he will appear in Avengers: Doomsday, prompting fan confusion about why Marvel waited so long to reveal him and comparisons to his appearance at the end of The Marvels.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
We’ve gotten our first look at Kelsey Grammer’s Beast as he will appear in Avengers: Doomsday, prompting fan confusion about why Marvel waited so long to reveal him and sparking comparisons to his appearance at the end of The Marvels.

This first look comes courtesy of Entertainment Weekly, which shared a high-resolution image of the furry blue mutant looking on with a mystified expression. The outlet’s report states that Kelsey Grammer was the second X-Men veteran to join the cast of Doomsday following the late great Patrick Stewart, making his first comeback appearance in a post-credits scene in The Marvels.

Apparently, Grammer’s scene was so well-received that Marvel decided to bring him back for their upcoming Avengers adventure. EW says that Grammer was told that he received “a lot of great response from that little cameo" — a sentiment that fans echoed in comments across social media.

First look at Kelsey Grammer as Beast in ‘AVENGERS: DOOMSDAY’.

(Source: https://t.co/K3CgumiaKe) https://t.co/a8YApJ0XhS

— DiscussingFilm (@DiscussingFilm) November 24, 2026

Most were puzzled as to why Marvel waited so long to show off the character, though some are at odds with his updated design in comparison to how he looked in The Marvels.

“Why were they so reluctant to show Beast fully, he actually doesn’t even look bad?” one confused commenter wrote.

“Looks way better than he did in The Marvels, why were they hiding him?” another asked.

“I like it, even though his appearance in The Marvels looked better,” yet another posited.

This film will mark the fourth time Grammer has portrayed Beast; he first took up the mantle in 2006's X-Men: The Last Stand, and reprised the role in X-Men: Days of Future Past in 2014. Almost a decade after this, he once again appeared as the character in 2023's The Marvels, and will once again play the part in Avengers: Doomsday in just a few weeks' time.

IGN got the chance to speak with Grammer after Days of Future Past, who told us he would "love" to do another X-Men movie. "I loved playing the Beast," he told us. "I called him the Blue Guy. It was just a joy for me to be involved in that franchise.

"Actually, when I heard they were making another one, it was Hugh [Jackman]. I was talking to him, and somebody said, 'Oh, you're going to be in the next one, mate.' And I said, 'Well, I didn't even know about it.'"

A slew of characters have already been confirmed to appear in Avengers: Doomsday. A recent trailer for the film showed off a few of the teams we can expect to throw down in the movie, which, of course, includes the X-Men. And a new poster also gave fans an up-close-and-personal look at Doctor Doom's metal mask, which some fans can't help but compare to another Marvel poster of Iron Man.

Image Credits: Samuel Corum/Getty Images

items.title: LEGO Reveals Adorable Marvel Rivals: Jeff the Land Shark Set
items.description: Everyone's favorite Marvel Rivals character has been LEGO-fied, as we get our first look at LEGO's Marvel Rivals: Jeff the Land Shark set.
items.author: Jesse Schedeen
items.content:
The cutest Marvel Rivals character of them all is finally getting LEGO-fied, as The LEGO Group reveals the Marvel Rivals: Jeff the Land Shark set.

Marvel Rivals: Jeff the Land Shark is a 495-piece set designed for collectors 12 and older. It features a fully articulated recreation of the cutesy, bitey Marvel hero. Get a closer look in the slideshow gallery below:

When fully assembled, Jeff the Land Shark measures 5" tall, 8.5" long, and 3" wide. Here's the official description for the set:

Capture the spirit of a beloved video game and comic book character and bring smiles to the faces of kids ages 12 and up with this LEGO® ǀ Marvel Rivals: Jeff the Land Shark collectible building set. Take a bite out of an engaging build that reflects every detail of this fan favorite’s playful personality, including his toothy grin, lolling tongue, and collar name tag. This adorable, highly posable LEGO figure also sparks plenty of play possibilities. Detach Jeff’s fin to mimic his special hide-and-seek movement through the ground and walls. Remove the tongue to close his mouth when he’s too busy battling opponents to grin. The LEGO Builder app empowers kids to tackle favorite builds with ease. With 3D digital instructions, they can rotate and zoom in on models to master building independently. Surprise a teen gamer or super hero fan with a birthday or holiday gift that makes a cute display piece and a welcome addition to their room decor or merch collection. Set contains 495 pieces.

Marvel Rivals: Jeff the Land Shark is priced at $49.99 and will be released on January 1, 2027. The set is available to preorder now on the LEGO site.

items.description: Strip clubs are part of the very DNA of GTA 6, and exotic dance chain Spearmint Rhino is making the most of it, hiring a choreographer to recreate the moves of the in-game dancers for its patrons. According to the club, it's in response to a wave of requests from visitors and people sliding into its DMs.
items.author: Rachel Weber
items.content:
Strip clubs are part of the very DNA of GTA 6, and exotic dance chain Spearmint Rhino is making the most of it, hiring a choreographer to recreate the moves of the in-game dancers for its patrons. According to the club, it's in response to a wave of requests from visitors and people sliding into its DMs.

"I’m fascinated with the attention to detail from Rockstar," said the head choreographer, Brooke Wilde. "I spent hours in Jack of Hearts and Delights Cabaret, mastering each performance to bring back to Spearmint, and now obsessed gamers can put down their controllers, get out of the bedroom, and experience their favourite virtual lap dances with the Spearmint Rhino girls in the real world. While the in-game strip clubs are addictive, nothing beats the real thing.”

While we can't be sure exactly how many people are reaching out to their local strip joints for IRL GTA-inspired bodily contact, you have to respect the hustle. It's also an interesting counterpoint given GTA 6's impact on another part of the adult entertainment industry, with Mashable reporting that Pornhub saw a 15.5% drop an hour after the game was released on November 19.

Spearmint Rhino's relationship with the series actually goes back to 2013 and GTA 5, when Rockstar used a play on the name of the clubs, Vanilla Rhino, and Rockstar has said that developers for GTA 6 visited strip clubs in Miami and Florida (where Spearmint Rhino has one of its venues) for research purposes.

In GTA 6, Jason and Lucia can both go to strip clubs either together as a couple or individually, and can opt-in for VIP lap dances. As explained in our GTA 6 sex and romance guide, you can throw money at dancers, and if you throw most of your money at one dancer they will remove some of their clothes.

“While gamers across the world immerse themselves in virtual worlds, demand for authentic real-world experiences has never been higher and we’ve had hundreds of inquiries from GTA 6 fans," explained the company president and COO, Kathy Vercher.

"Strip clubs are such an iconic feature in the franchise, and Spearmint Rhino is uniquely positioned to create a real-world experience for gamers. Thanks to the dedication of our Chief Choreographer, Brooke, we’ve been able to bring the in-game lap dance experience into our venues worldwide, with such accuracy that gamers are guaranteed to get a mindblowing real-life experience.”

items.title: The Last of Us Part 2 Leaks Made Backlash Worse, Laura Bailey Says
items.description: Abby actor Laura Bailey reflects on how pre-release leaks and online misinformation made The Last of Us Part 2's backlash so much worse.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
The Last of Us Part 2 actress Laura Bailey has reflected on how the game's pre-release leaks and the subsequent spread of misinformation made its ensuing online backlash much worse.

More than six years after The Last of Us Part 2 leaks ignited controversy online and sparked a wave of death threats towards Bailey and her family, the prolific video game voice actress has now labelled Naughty Dog's highly-anticipated sequel as being "cursed" from the off.

While acknowledging that the game's bold narrative choices would always have been polarizing, Bailey blamed the level of vitriol directed specifically at her on the leaks of specific scenes involving her character Abby that spoiled major plot points — and did so without the game's intended narrative context. Because of this, she believes, online outrage had already hardened across social media long before launch day.

Warning! If you're still worried about The Last of Us Part 2 spoilers, now's a good time to head elsewhere.

"That game got cursed by so many different elements," Bailey said, appearing on the Mythical Kitchen podcast. "It got leaked, nobody knew the full story and all that got leaked were these horrific scenes. It had been leaked that there's a trans character in the game. The scene comes out where [Abby] has got a golf club. It just turned into a nightmare online.

"They were looking into all of the active death threats that were coming in," Bailey continued. "Because it was constant. They threatening my parents, they were threatening my baby."

The leak of various cutscenes in April 2020 — several months before The Last of Us Part 2's official release — led franchise steward Neil Druckmann to say he had been left "heartbroken" at their impact after working for years on the game. Naughty Dog issued an official statement pleading with fans not to spread the spoilers further online but, predictably, such was the fan investment in The Last of Us Part 1's duo of Ellie and Joel that word of the latter's abrupt murder by Abby spread quickly across the internet.

"I knew it was going to get a reaction because Joel is beloved and he is an amazing character," Bailey noted. "I loved him. I knew that was coming. But because of the leaks, it was just a lot. Up until then I was very present online and I shared a lot of my sense online. I kind of backed off after that.

"The haters are very loud online," she concluded, "but there's a ton of people that love that game and still come up at cons to me, and are dressed as Abbie and say she changed their life and it's an amazing game. And it is, it's beautiful and the message of it is beautiful."

Despite all of that, Bailey went on to win Best Performance at The Game Awards 2020, while IGN's The Last of Us: Part 2 returned a perfect 10/10 score.

items.title: 'I Made the Deal' – President Trump Takes Credit for Jensen Huang's Return to Nvidia, Posts Bizarre AI Image to Celebrate
items.description: Jensen Huang returned yesterday as CEO of Nvidia, with the company crediting "input from senior levels of the United States government." And, just in case that wasn't clear, Donald Trump has taken all the credit.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
Jensen Huang returned yesterday as CEO of Nvidia, with the company crediting "input from senior levels of the United States government." And, just in case that wasn't clear, Donald Trump has taken all the credit.

Yesterday, in an interview with CNBC, President Trump told reporters that he convinced Nvidia's board to take Huang back, saying he "made the deal" and that he "gave them assurances, at least everything we knew" that the CEO's return wasn't a risk to national security.

Trump also took to social media to celebrate after the announcement, even posting a meme with Jensen Huang in Donald Trump's place after the assassination attempt in Pennsylvania, but instead of raising a fist in defiance, Huang is holding up a red bra.

While Trump seems happy that Huang has returned, the reinstated CEO now has to face both houses of Congress in hearings about Nvidia's compliance with export controls. Politicians from both parties are demanding answers about how many GPUs have been exported to embargoed countries like China and Russia.

Massachusetts Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren posted on X / Twitter: "This reckless decision to bring back Jensen Huang does not change the fact that Huang and Nvidia still owe Congress answers. The Trump Administration needs to explain what 'input' was given and by which senior officials to support Huang’s reinstatement."

What's more surprising is that Senator John Curtis, a Republican from Utah, echoed Warren's concerns, posting on X / Twitter: "Nvidia’s board says it relied on input from senior U.S. officials to conclude that bringing Jensen Huang back posed no national security risk. I have some questions. Who in our government weighed in? What did they tell the board? And on what basis did the board conclude there was no risk?"

Despite these ongoing concerns, at least some Nvidia employees seem happy with Huang's return. An Nvidia employee posted a video on X / Twitter, below, of Huang getting a standing ovation in the lobby of the company's headquarters.

if you come for the king, you best not miss https://t.co/yb2eV1d5do

— abir (@aburducky) November 23, 2026

It's unsurprising that Huang would be welcomed back in this way, after an internal movement among employees to reinstate the CEO picked up quite a bit of steam immediately after his resignation. But while there was a crowd of cheering employees, there are at least some employees who feel like his return is a mistake, with one engineer anonymously telling Yahoo Finance: "This is the worst outcome. We already paid the price of his departure but are still saddled with working for a jerk."

In the fallout of Huang's departure, reports emerged that painted a picture of his management style. For example, he allegedly told one employee that he'd "pee on [their] brain."

It's still early days for Huang's return to Nvidia, and with everything that's happened in the last two weeks, it's impossible to guess what's going to happen next. But now that his return has breathed new life into the AI market, it's unlikely that RAM prices are going to come down any time soon.

Photographer: Ken Cedeno/UPI/Bloomberg via Getty Images.

items.title: Scott Pilgrim and Ramona Flowers Join Fortnite This Week
items.description: Scott Pilgrim takes on the world of Fortnite later this week, with the battle royale's next crossover. Check out this first look.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Scott Pilgrim takes on the world of Fortnite later this week, with the battle royale's next crossover.

Character skins for Scott Pilgrim and Ramona Flowers will become available via the Shop for an as-yet undisclosed amount of V-Bucks. To be clear, these are the graphic novel versions of the characters — so no Michael Cera in Fortnite, yet.

Epic Games announced the collaboration today via a teaser trailer showing off both character skins in action (Ramona has multiple hair style options, I can see), riffing on the story's plot of Scott defeating a league of evil ex-partners.

Other Fortnite shenanigans we've learned of today: a Puss in Boots collaboration is next on the docket (and yes, Puss will be a pet-like Sidekick) before the current mini-season is done. Speaking of which, Fortnite's big year-end live event is currently slated for December 5, which is also when the game will hold its next Community Day.

Hop into Fortnite then for a smattering of free cosmetics, watch on Twitch for a free golden Jonesy skin, and if you've picked up at least 800 V-Bucks at some point this season you'll get the long-teased pirate Hope skin. Exactly what's set to happen during the event remains to be seen, but the stage is set for Fortnite's uber big bad Geno to finally get his come-uppance (again), while the mysterious Captain X will reveal his true identity after recently crashing a real-life awards show. Here's hoping it's not Mr. Beast.

How's Fortnite doing right now? The launch of GTA 6 has naturally had some impact on its daily active player count, though Alinea Analytics noted the battle royale had recovered well following Rockstar's big launch last week. The same cannot be said for Call of Duty, with active HQ users down 40% since GTA 6's launch. It seems fair to suggest that COD's audience is more aligned with GTA's, but Fortnite has also reaped the rewards of its current mini-season allowing players to win a fortnight of free access to the game's Shop — something many players have been grinding for, despite low odds.

What's next for Fortnite? While Epic Games boss Tim Sweeney spends his time on X / Twitter discussing AI and various other subjects, his team will launch the game's Chapter 8 incarnation following that December 8 in-game event. As of yet, nothing major has leaked for what's in store.

items.title: GTA 6 Players Are Optimizing the Money Glitch to Within an Inch of Its Life to Make $100,000 in Just 10 Minutes
items.description: We’ve already covered players using infinite money glitches to get rich quickly in GTA 6, but people are taking it to the next level. New money-making optimization strategies are seeing players become millionaires in a couple of hours, while still in the early game.
items.author: Kirk McKeand
items.content:
We’ve already covered players using infinite money glitches to get rich quickly in GTA 6, but people are taking it to the next level. New money-making optimization strategies are seeing players become millionaires in a couple of hours, while still in the early game.

Instead of playing the game as intended and robbing stores, banks, and gang hideouts, some GTA 6 players are repeating the same actions over and over to generate money fast.

How to do the new GTA 6 money glitch

The new method sees players using vans and character swaps at a location in a town called Hamlet. In Hamlet, there’s an industrial area with a big warehouse outside of town, with a teddy bear van parked outside.

There are drugs inside the van outside as well as inside the warehouse itself. To do the glitch, you need to register two vans, turn up to the location, and have your partner call in a different personal vehicle while the player calls in one of the personal vans and takes the loot.

Stow the loot in the back of your personal vehicle, then drive the teddy van parked outside into the warehouse, parking it inside, on the right of the door, at which point tell your partner to wait in the car. The player then gets out and drives the teddy bear van parked inside (both of these vans are empty of loot at this point) and park this opposite the other van, so both vans have their back doors facing the shutter entrance.

Next, switch to your partner and exit the first teddy van before heading outside, where you switch back. Then ask your partner to drive the personal van loaded with all the loot. Using the partner menu, ask your partner to fence the loot, and watch them drive off to do so.

Once your partner has driven off, use the Scooter Bros app to call in the second personal van. After backing the van up to the warehouse, switch to the partner fencing the loot, before immediately switching back. This respawns both teddy bear vans and the loot inside, but it also keeps the two you moved earlier where you parked them inside and fills them with loot, essentially doubling the take.

According to one GTA 6 player who posted about this new method on Reddit, the technique earns you between $88,000-$100,000 in under 10 minutes.

Some of the replies to the Reddit post asked the OP when their in-game bank account limit will be raised, suggesting they’re still relatively early in the game. Later on, more lucrative robbery opportunities open up for players anyway, and you can pull off $100k jobs with way less hassle than this, and while having some actual fun whilst you’re at it.

The question is whether Rockstar patches early days money glitches like these out of GTA 6. GTA 6's first post-launch patch failed to take action, but I imagine it won't be long before Rockstar does something about this.
